decision: Apply the named Rødenes church building geometry and bind it to the correct church, heritage and address identities while rejecting the former-municipality entity.
identityFindings: OSM way 957797045 represents the Rødenes church building and gives representative point 59.58808, 11.59488.
Wikimedia Commons identifies the church building as Wikidata Q6494543 and Norwegian heritage ID 85331, with address Rødenes Kirkevei 174.
Wikidata Q7386714 represents the former Rødenes municipality and must not be used as the church-building identity, even where an external map aggregate exposes that association.
The public information point south of the church is a visitor component, not the canonical building anchor.
chronologyFindings: Marker municipality dates the Romanesque stone church to around 1230.
The Church of Norway describes it more cautiously as built in the first half of the thirteenth century.
Some registry metadata uses 1275; this is not adopted as a certain exact construction year.
The church was lengthened and substantially altered in 1703–1709, receiving the present tower, porch and sacristy.
Medieval roof construction and parts of the eastern gables remain preserved.

siteContext.setting: Headland on the western side of Rødenessjøen, east of the rectory

rejectedAlternatives.reason: Geographically close but lacks an explicit building and entity contract.
Identifies the former Rødenes municipality, not the church building.
Represents public interpretation rather than the church building.
Would represent wider site context rather than the protected medieval building.

representationLimits: The marker represents the church building, while the churchyard, rectory and lakeside setting are wider contexts.
The radius is not a building, churchyard, heritage, property, shoreline or event boundary.
Services, funerals, cemetery use and other current church activities take precedence over gameplay.
Year 1230 is approximate and must not be treated as an exact documented construction date.
